blocks.text: Isaiah 61 has been read in diverse ways. A responsible interpretation first considers the chapter's own literary sense and historical referent, then distinguishes that question from claims about prediction, typology, quotation or allusion, wider canonical synthesis, Jewish reception, or later christological and ecclesial readings.

The Great Isaiah Scroll is an almost complete witness to all sixty-six chapters of Isaiah. It broadly aligns with the Masoretic tradition while also containing many spelling and substantive differences; other Qumran Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings likewise show active transmission and interpretation of the book.
